assessments.technical_explanation: The serialize-environment signal is triggered by spreading process.env into the spawn options for a local helper script. This is standard Node.js practice to inherit the parent environment while adding a port override. The child process is a known local test server script within the same repository. No environment data is exfiltrated or sent to any external destination; it is passed locally to a trusted child process.
assessments.layman_explanation: The test script launches a local helper program and passes along its own environment settings so the helper can run correctly. This is normal and expected for a test tool. No sensitive information leaves the machine.

assessments.technical_explanation: The scanner flagged a fixed string at line 158 as a suspicious link. The actual value is the standard SVG namespace URI passed to document.createElementNS, which is a mandatory constant for creating SVG elements in the DOM. No network request is made to this URI; it is a namespace identifier, not a destination. The surrounding code builds SVG polyline and path elements for visual callout layout and cohesion ring rendering. There is no network access, credential handling, or data exfiltration present.
assessments.layman_explanation: The scanner saw a web address in the code, but it is just the official identifier the browser requires to create SVG graphics. No data is sent anywhere; it is a standard part of drawing on-screen visuals.

assessments.technical_explanation: The scanner correlates a network retrieval primitive with an execution sink in the same file. The fetch calls target only a localhost preview server on a dynamically chosen port, used to wait for the server to become ready. The spawn call launches a known local repository script for that same preview server. No remote or untrusted content is downloaded and then executed; both the fetch destination and the spawned program are local and repo-internal. This is standard Playwright test harness orchestration.
assessments.layman_explanation: The test script starts a local mini-server and then checks that it is running before proceeding with visual tests. The scanner flagged this because it sees both a network check and a program launch in the same file, but both are local and part of the test setup. Nothing dangerous is happening.

assessments.technical_explanation: The scanner matched a credential-to-network rule at line 234 where connection.send('Page.navigate', { url: BASE_URL }) is called. BASE_URL is defined as process.env.SILLYTAVERN_BASE_URL or a default of a localhost address on port 8000. It is a base URL for a local SillyTavern server instance, not a credential or secret. The script is a tooling-only visual capture utility that launches a headless browser via CDP, navigates to the local SillyTavern instance, opens the Directive runtime panel, navigates to specific UI routes, captures screenshots, and writes layout metrics to the docs directory. No credentials, API keys, or sensitive user data are read or transmitted. The environment variable controls a local server address, and all network activity is to localhost. The file role is tooling and execution scope is tooling-only, so this code does not run in the shipped extension.
assessments.layman_explanation: The scanner flagged code that sends a value to a network function, but the value is just the address of the user's own local SillyTavern server. This is a developer screenshot tool that opens a local test page and takes pictures for design documentation. No passwords or secrets are involved, and this tool is not part of what users install.

assessments.technical_explanation: The encoded-literal signal at line 1147 corresponds to a SHA-256 digest hex string used as an expected assertion value in a visual conformance test. The test computes a hash of image pixel data and compares it against this known-good fixture value. This is a deterministic test fixture, not obfuscation or hidden data. The string is a plain hex digest embedded for assertion purposes.

observations.title: SVG namespace URI used in createElementNS calls
observations.technical_explanation: The same standard SVG namespace URI appears in multiple createElementNS calls throughout the file for creating svg, polyline, and path elements. These are standard DOM API calls for SVG rendering and carry no network semantics.
observations.layman_explanation: The code uses the standard web address needed to draw SVG graphics in several places. This is normal browser programming, not network communication.
